        "text": "**Analyzing Thermal Overrides**\n\nMy current thinking revolves around the implications of unchecking the \"Temperature Limit\" option within UXTU.       "text": "If you uncheck (turn off) the **Temperature Limit** toggle in UXTU (Universal x86 Tuning Utility):\n\n### 1. It reverts to the factory default (BIOS / OEM) limit\nTurning the toggle off does **not** remove thermal protection. It simply stops UXTU from overriding the limit, handing control back to your laptop\u0027s default firmware (HP Victus / AMD BIOS defaults). \n\n### 2. Your CPU will still protect itself from overheating\nModern processors have hard-coded hardware protections that software cannot disable:\n* **Default soft throttling (TjMax):** For modern AMD Ryzen mobile APUs, the factory limit is typically between **95°C and 100°C** (or 105°C depending on the exact chip). The processor will automatically dial back clock speeds if it reaches this threshold.\n* **Emergency shutdown:** If temperatures were ever to exceed critical safe levels (usually around 105°C–115°C), the laptop will immediately shut down to prevent physical damage.\n\n---\n\n### What to expect in practice:\n* **If HP’s default limit is already ~95°C–100°C:** You likely won\u0027t notice much difference.\n* **Why keep it enabled?** The main reason to check this box is if you want to set a **lower** target (e.g., 85°C–90°C) to keep fan noise down and lap/keyboard temperatures cooler with only a negligible loss in gaming performance. Setting it to 95°C (as shown in your screenshot) is already very close to the standard AMD mobile factory behavior.",
